svg.title: Figure 5-8. Loss scenarios: openpilot's control actions (C2) (WP-A-05 §5)
svg.desc: Figure 5-8: 12 loss scenario cards for openpilot's control actions (C2). LS-01 (UCA-10, Known gap): The driver steers against the item to avoid an obstacle. Driver torque only freezes the integrator; 'overriding' is an active state, and the panda limits have no driver-torque term. The item keeps commanding torque against the driver. Back-off and cue decided, not implemented; thresholds wait on DQ-081 and AOU-02R. LS-06 (UCA-19, Covered): The driver presses SET while openpilot is not ready; the PCM engages cruise. Until v0.3 the panda granted authority on the PCM edge; now only once the heartbeat reports openpilot engaged. Acceleration or torque while openpilot is not engaged but cruise is. Covered since v0.3.1: authority only once openpilot reports engaged; open test for the PCM response (OI-4). LS-09 (UCA-18, UCA-05, Known gap): Sunglasses or low light lower driver-monitoring confidence. The policy falls back to wheel touch (5/15/25 s) while the driver looks at a phone. Up to 25 s, several hundred metres, unsupervised; speed escalation (TSR-634) is unit-tested only. Speed-dependent wheel-touch escalation decided (DQ-077 A) and required by TSR-634; implemented (SWSR-634, unit tests only), not yet validated in the vehicle (WP-V-02 §4.4); the speed table is in WP-C-08 §5.4. LS-10 (UCA-11, Known gap): Lane lines are faded or misleading (construction). The model plans a wrong curvature; the torque stays within the envelope, so the panda does not act. The car leaves its lane; the driver is the only control. SOTIF residual: model error inside the envelope, controlled by the driver and argued by validation. LS-12 (UCA-20, UCA-58, Covered): A wrong fingerprint selects another platform. The reference lock stops a wrong brand or parameter, but another Toyota with scale 73 gets the right limits and wrong tuning. The wrong safety mode or parameter is sent to the panda. Covered in the default build; known gap for same-parameter Toyotas and for the opt-out build. LS-16 (UCA-12, Known gap): The item stops steering in a curve. The saturation warning needs three conditions and is suppressed for 2 s after any steering press. No torque in the curve and no alert. Saturation warning suppressed 2 s after a steering press, no FTTI row; TSR-604 partly implemented. LS-17 (UCA-14, UCA-52, Known gap): The driving model misses a stationary or slower lead in Chill Mode. The planner plans acceleration; the panda knows nothing of leads and passes up to +2.0 m/s². The car accelerates toward the lead. SOTIF residual: the envelope has no lead information. LS-18 (UCA-15, UCA-51, New finding): A cut-in or a slowing lead is detected late. The leads come from the driving model, so the same miss removes planner braking and the FCW together. Deceleration comes too late, and is capped at −3.5 m/s². New: the SG-06 tree has events for a lost plan, not a late one (§6). LS-19 (UCA-16, Known gap): A false lead brakes hard. The envelope passes any in-bound step and has no jerk limit. Hard deceleration without a real obstacle. Not implemented; jerk values wait on DQ-081. LS-20 (UCA-17, Known gap): A take-over request is not perceived. Every alert goes through ui and soundd, so a hung HMI mutes them; the panda siren covers heartbeat loss and EPS faults only. The take-over alert is not given when control is lost. HMI liveness supervision and the SOFT_DISABLE review not implemented. LS-34 (UCA-63, Covered): On a radar-ACC platform, alpha longitudinal disables the stock radar ECU over UDS. That turns PCS off; since v0.4 card refuses the alpha request on any vehicle. The stock radar, and with it PCS/AEB, is silenced. Covered: unit-tested, not verified on a vehicle; applies to every non-reference platform. LS-35 (UCA-21, Known gap): The driver falls asleep or becomes unwell. Alerts escalate to level three; 5 s later the car brakes towards a stop in the lane, on the same QM chain. No specified and assured minimal-risk behaviour. Reaction decided (DQ-365, TSR-633) and implemented in software, not verified on the vehicle: 5 s after the last alert the car stops in the lane, the stop is latched until the driver takes over, it cannot resume, and the lockout runs from the takeover; there is still no announcement before it starts (TSR-624), the hold rests on the untested AOU-16 (UE-8.11), and the forced stop is a single point in the SG-08 tree (MCS-08.7).
